message.content: The common ancestor of lions (family Felidae) and zebras (family Equidae) is a member of the order Carnivora that lived around 50–60 million years ago. This ancestor was a small, omnivorous mammal that gave rise to the diverse lineages of modern carnivores, including the felids (cats) and the perissodactyls (odd-toed ungulates).
